crawled_in_feedback_era_without_success.does_not_show: why: an empty feed, URLs already stored, only short or discarded pages and a read error swallowed by the legacy code all look the same. Only the first feed of a source to list a new URL in a run was credited (feeds were read by score, priority, update time), so a feed that duplicates a better-ranked feed of the same outlet lands here although it lists good URLs. A run aborted before the feedback step leaves no stamp either
crawled_in_feedback_era_without_success.shows: the feed was read by a crawl at or after the first recorded last_success_at and no success was ever stamped on it

discovery_verdict_only.does_not_show: a crawl result: the verdict is one probe of at most 8 URLs with the legacy extractor, or an HTTP status seen once
discovery_verdict_only.shows: no crawl read the feed in the feedback era; the last discovery scoring left a non-active verdict (see fail_category)

last_success_at_set.does_not_show: how often: the table keeps only the last success per feed and nothing links an article to the feed that listed it, so a repetition cannot be attributed to this feed
last_success_at_set.shows: the feed listed at least one URL that became an 'ok' article (>= 100 extracted words) in the crawl run that wrote last_success_at

no_crawl_and_no_verdict.shows: no crawl in the feedback era, no success stamp and no discovery failure reason

sitemap_index_not_expanded_by_legacy.does_not_show: anything about what the index leads to
sitemap_index_not_expanded_by_legacy.shows: the feed is a sitemap index; the legacy scorer never activated one and the crawl service skipped them

sole_successful_feed_of_source_with_repe.does_not_show: an inference, not a per-feed log: a feed deleted from the table since, or a crawl through another code path, would break it; it says nothing about the channel today
sole_successful_feed_of_source_with_repe.shows: last_success_at is set, no other feed row of the same legacy source has it set, and the source finished with saved > 0 in crawl runs of the feedback era on two or more distinct days; each such finish stamped at least one feed, so by exclusion it was this one

channel_class_order: last_success_at set, the only such feed of its source, source success on >= 2 run days in the feedback era -> PRODUCTIVE_REPEATED
last_crawled_at or last_attempt_at >= feedback era start -> NEVER_SUCCESSFUL
rules.directory_mapping: <COUNTRY>/<slug> equals (country_code, newspaper_code) of a legacy source, else its ASCII fold equals the ASCII fold of exactly one newspaper_code of that country, else unmapped

feedback_era.meaning: feeds.last_success_at is the only per-feed success record. Its earliest value bounds from above the moment the legacy crawl feedback began; a crawl before 'start' could not stamp a feed, so only crawls from 'start' on count as evidence for or against a feed.

rules.legacy_crawl_eligible_at_snapshot: is_active = 1 and status = 'active' and feed_score >= 40 and type != 'sitemap_index' (the legacy crawl service's filter)
rules.on_disk: names and sizes from a directory listing; no file opened. The date in a file name is the legacy date_published of the records in it, not a fetch date. 'backup' is listed for completeness; its directory names predate the ASCII slug migration.

outlet_class.LEGACY_NEVER_PRODUCTIVE: feed rows or article rows exist, no 'ok' row
outlet_class.LEGACY_NO_CHANNEL: no feed row and no article row
outlet_class.LEGACY_PRODUCTIVE_REPEATED: articles rows with status 'ok' in crawl runs that each gave >= 5 'ok' rows for the outlet, on >= 2 distinct days (day of the run's first 'ok' fetch for the outlet)
outlet_class.LEGACY_PRODUCTIVE_SPORADIC: at least one 'ok' row, but not the above
outlet_class.note: the two parameters are choices of this audit, not legacy values; the counts they are applied to are in every record, so another threshold can be applied without a re-run. 'ok' is the legacy status for >= 100 extracted words. Repeated is not lasting: see last_ok_fetch_day.

rules.source_success_run: a crawl run of the feedback era whose source_results_json lists the source with saved > 0; the run day is the date of crawl_runs.started_at
rules.times: all legacy stamps are naive datetime.utcnow() values, compared as strings

cross.note: the two figures answer different questions (feed state at the snapshot vs. files left by past exports) and must not be equated or subtracted from one another

newspapers_without_active_feed.definition: A-D count rows of the legacy sources table by the state of their feed rows at the snapshot. B is the reading 'no feed with is_active = 1'. B includes A. None of them counts outlets without articles or without files.

outlet_directories_with_json_raw_materia.definition: directories <COUNTRY>/<slug> under json_raw that hold at least one *.json file, by listing. A directory is not an outlet: two directories can belong to one outlet and a directory can match no legacy source.
